title: Is China Backing Out?? Tough Talk on US Ag Purchases Following Blue Wave Election

bullets: China says it will buy more US ag only once the $30B-for-$30B tariff-cut deal is implemented. The video frames the deal as at risk
China’s non-soy US ag purchases were $7.2B through September, the lowest for that period since 2019
Flash sale: 167k MT (~6 mbu) soybeans to Spain, 26/27 delivery
US soybean sales are running ~80% ahead of last year’s pace
Ethanol output was 1.14m bpd, the second-highest on record (+2.2% w/w)
Jan beans fell ~12c to ~12.02, the lowest since mid-August, on weaker crude and the big-crop outlook
Dec corn rose 2c to 4.44 on an oversold bounce
Wheat was lower on hopes for Russia–Ukraine peace talks
Rabobank sees Brazil’s soy crop at 178 MMT, vs USDA’s record 186. It expects exports to dip to 113 MMT
Rabobank cites rising costs, tight margins and El Niño
WTI fell 8.3% to $88.12, its lowest close since late August, on US–Iran deal hopes after Democrats took both chambers. Some analysts call the drop overdone
There’s a chapter on Vance comments, but the description doesn’t say what was said
Deere is closing its Ottumwa and Clarion, Iowa plants and moving sugar cane harvester production to Brazil
USDA and CFTC signed an agreement on oversight and data sharing
Commitments of Traders reports go twice weekly starting December
